newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE TO GET NEW INDEPENDENT SUNDAY NEWSPAPER.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE TO GET NEW INDEPENDENT SUNDAY NEWSPAPER.

text.p: Zimbabwe, whose media is dominated by the state, is set to get an independent Sunday newspaper in April, the paper's sponsors said.

Clive Murphy and Clive Wilson said in a statement late on Thursday their company, Sovereign Publishers, would launch The Zimbabwe Standard on April 13, almost a year after they launched the southern African state's second independent financial weekly, The Zimbabwe Independent.
"The new paper aims to provide bright, informative weekend reading, without any political or sectoral association," said Mark Chavunduka, editor-designate of The Zimbabwe Standard.

There are currently two Sunday newspapers in the country, both published by the largely state-owned and officially- controlled Zimbabwe Newspapers group, which also publishes the nation's only two dailies.
